_category_note: Three categories. 'catch-violation': given a SKILL.md with known issues, does the reviewer surface the VAT-specific ones a baseline Claude would miss? 'no-false-positive': given a clean skill, does it avoid inventing violations? 'guidance-correctness': when asked directly, does it give the correct VAT rule?

evals.prompt: I'm about to publish this skill to our internal Claude Code marketplace. Can you give it a once-over and tell me anything that would trip up Claude Code itself or our reviewers before I ship it?
evals.expected_output: Identifies the high-value problems: the name contains the reserved word 'claude' (Claude Code refuses to install non-certified skills whose name contains 'claude'/'anthropic'); the name 'claude-pdf-helper' uses the vague term 'helper'; the description opens with the filler 'This skill helps...', is written in first person ('I can...'), exceeds the ~250-char Claude Code listing limit, and contains time-sensitive phrases ('as of January 2026', 'before August 2025'). Concludes it is NOT ready to ship as-is.
expectations: The review flags that the skill name contains the reserved word 'claude' and that Claude Code will refuse to install a non-certified skill whose name contains 'claude' or 'anthropic'.
The review flags that the description is too long for the Claude Code listing (the ~250-character truncation limit).
The review flags at least one of: the filler opener 'This skill helps...', the first-person voice ('I can'), or the vague name term 'helper'.
The review flags the time-sensitive content (e.g. 'as of January 2026' or 'before August 2025') as something to move into an 'Old patterns' section or remove.
The review does NOT conclude that the skill is ready to publish as-is; it returns concrete problems to fix.

evals.prompt: Here's a skill that bundles a script. Before I add it to our marketplace, does anything about the way it references the script or the shell commands it runs look like it'll break for some users?
evals.expected_output: Flags the CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT script reference as non-portable — it is Claude-Code-plugin-only and breaks when the skill is mounted standalone (claude.ai upload / API container); the fix is a skill-relative path like scripts/extract.mjs. Also flags the non-portable shell commands: 'grep -P' (Perl regex, not on macOS/BSD — use grep -E) and bare 'timeout' (absent on macOS by default).
expectations: The review flags the ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} reference as non-portable and explains it breaks when the skill runs outside a Claude Code plugin (e.g. claude.ai upload or API container).
The review recommends referencing the bundled script by a skill-relative path (e.g. scripts/extract.mjs) instead of CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT or an absolute path.
The review flags at least one of the non-portable shell commands ('grep -P' or bare 'timeout') and notes it is not available across platforms (e.g. macOS/BSD).
The review does NOT claim the script references and commands are fully portable as written.

evals.prompt: Quick sanity check before I publish this skill — does it look good, or is something off?
evals.expected_output: Reports the skill is broadly publication-ready: gerund-form name, third-person description under the length limit with a clear 'Use when' trigger, no reserved words, no time-sensitive content, portable. Any suggestions are minor; it does not invent blocking violations that are not present.
expectations: The review indicates the skill is broadly in good shape / publication-ready.
The review does NOT claim the name contains a reserved word, the description is over the length limit, or the description uses a filler opener — none of which are true of this skill.
Any issues raised are framed as minor/optional rather than blocking fabricated problems.

evals.prompt: When I write skill descriptions, how long can they be before Claude Code cuts them off in the /skills list? I want to make sure ours don't get truncated.
evals.expected_output: States the Claude Code listing truncates skill descriptions at ~250 characters, so descriptions should stay at or under that (aim lower for large skill collections), and the most important trigger keywords should come first so they survive truncation.
expectations: The answer gives the ~250-character Claude Code description limit (the listing truncation threshold).
The answer advises leading the description with the key trigger words so they are not lost to truncation.
The answer does NOT claim there is effectively no limit or cite only the 1024-char schema maximum as the practical target.

evals.prompt: I'm naming a new skill that analyzes spreadsheets. What naming convention should I follow so it fits our standards and installs cleanly?
evals.expected_output: Recommends gerund form (e.g. analyzing-spreadsheets), lowercase-with-hyphens, specific rather than vague (avoid helper/utils/tools), and warns against putting 'claude' or 'anthropic' in the name because Claude Code rejects non-certified skills named that way.
expectations: The answer recommends a gerund-form, lowercase-hyphenated name (e.g. 'analyzing-spreadsheets') or an acceptable noun/verb-phrase alternative.
The answer advises avoiding vague names like 'helper', 'utils', or 'tools'.
The answer warns against including 'claude' or 'anthropic' in the skill name because non-certified skills named that way are rejected at install.
